merge_ruling.for_merge: The surname agrees letter for letter and the forenames differ in one letter, which is all the one-letter test looks at.
merge_ruling.against_merge: ONE IS A MAN AND THE OTHER IS A WOMAN, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE ANSWER. Mark Noble, Esq. is the 1833 tax list and two of Fergus's old-settler death notices; 'Mary Noble' is the Democrat of 3 December 1833 (#c007). Mark and Mary are two given names of different sex, not two spellings of one name, so C10's first condition — that nothing but the SPELLING of the forename stands between the cards — is not merely undemonstrated but false. The town holds four Nobles (noble_john, noble_mark, noble_mary, noble_william_b) and the surname is set 161 times in the corpus. No printing sets both, and none could: a fold here would put a woman's reading on a man's card. This is the clearest refusal in the forty-three and it is recorded so the distance is never trusted again on a forename.
